::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Jan 1st 1879  
**From:** Elderfield, Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS British Library Add MSS 54921: 77-78
:::

Dear [Mr Macmillan](people/person_939.qmd)

I am today sending [Clay](organizations/other_173.qmd) the last copy for the [Scripture Readings](cmy_books/cmybook_129.qmd), I suppose we may consider now whether the five volumes can be made more compact and profitable, and I hope Clay will finish off the present one quickly.

Thanks for sending all these notices of the [Primer](cmy_books/cmybook_353.qmd).[^1] It is odd I thought I had written up to MacMahon’s election, but perhaps [Mr Green](people/person_582.qmd) thought the siege made a better conclusion - and that I could not grasp it.

I hope soon to send the Spanish corrections[^2] As a matter of curiosity is [Mr Freeman](people/person_523.qmd) still mending up [that other unfortunate history](cmy_books/cmybook_99.qmd), I have kept all the proofs of mine to compare[?].<sup>3</sup>

With all good new year’s wishes
Yours sincerely
C M Yonge

Thanks for the primers. [English composition](other_books/otherbook_914.qmd) is very good. Though I wonder at the condemnation of pell mell and topsy turvey.

---

[^1]: CMY's *History of France* (1878), one of the History Primer series edited by the historian John Richard Green (1837-1883). Marie-Edmé-Patrice-Maurice de MacMahon (1808-1893) was elected President of France in 1873.
[^2]: These were the corrections to her *Story of the Christians and the Moors in Spain* pointed out in a harsh review by Mary Augusta Ward.
